The '''1994–95 season''' was the 64th season for '''[[Real Madrid CF|Real Madrid]]''' in [[La Liga]].

==Summary==
During the summer, the club was reinforced in the midfield with Danish playmaker [[Michael Laudrup]] (in a controversial transfer from [[FC Barcelona|Barcelona]]) and Argentine [[Fernando Redondo]];<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.goal.com/en/news/722/la-liga/2016/02/10/20197242/laudrup-why-i-left-barcelona-dream-team-for-real-madrid|title=Why I left Barcelona Dream Team for Real Madrid|language=es|publisher=goal.com|date=10 February 2016|access-date=2 August 2020}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.elespanol.com/elbernabeu/futbol/20190803/fernando-redondo-principe-argentina-imanes-botas/418738124_3.html|publisher=elespanol.com|title=Fernando Redondo Prince of Argentina|language=es|date=24 October 2014|access-date=2 August 2020}}</ref> right back defender [[Quique Sánchez Flores|Sánchez Flores]] arrived from [[Valencia CF|Valencia]],<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.elperiodico.com/es/deportes/20170217/la-banda-era-de-quique-5844910|title=The right back was for Quique|language=es|date=20 February 2017|publisher=elperiodico.com}}</ref> and changes came to the dugout too, with Argentine head coach [[Jorge Valdano]] arriving from [[CD Tenerife]] after seven years of his forced retirement as a player during the climax of "[[La Quinta del Buitre]]" era.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://elpais.com/diario/1994/12/23/agenda/788137203_850215.html|title=The Record of Valdano|work=El País|language=es|date=22 December 1994|access-date=2 August 2020}}</ref>

The team played a 4–4–2 system with Buyo remaining as goalkeeper, [[Quique Sánchez Flores]] replacing aging [[Chendo]] as right back, while the central defenders were [[Fernando Hierro]] and [[Manolo Sanchís]] who replaced an injured Alkorta, along with the left back [[Mikel Lasa]]. Valdano changed the midfield towards aggressive play with Redondo and Laudrup in the center, Amavisca played superb as left winger and [[Luis Enrique]] took the right wing, a new role for him that turned out to be crucial for the squad. In the attacking line, Zamorano recovered his high level of play after a disastrous campaign last season, winning the [[Pichichi Trophy]] as the league top scorer. The season also saw the breakthrough of a 17-year-old forward [[Raúl (footballer)|Raúl]] who would assume the starting position in place of rapidly declining [[Alfonso Pérez|Alfonso]] and [[Emilio Butragueño]].

In the meantime, financial worries increased during the season and on 16 February 1995, incumbent [[Ramon Mendoza]] defeated challenger [[Florentino Pérez]] in the club's longest ever Presidential election by just 698 votes. Mendoza's re-election was possible due to the good pace of the team in the [[1994–95 La Liga|league]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://as.com/futbol/2020/03/22/reportajes/1584870613_666387.html#:~:text=Ram%C3%B3n%20Mendoza%20gan%C3%B3%20las%20elecciones,marcha%20ahogado%20por%20la%20econom%C3%ADa.&text=LA%20%C3%BAltima%20directiva%20del%20Real,Villar%20Mir%20a%20su%20derecha.|publisher=as.com|title=Ramon Mendoza walked off drowned by debts|language=es|date=22 March 2020|access-date=2 August 2020}}</ref> Madrid ultimately clinched its first 26th league title and first in five years. In the cup competitions, however, the team was less fortunate, going out at the round of 16 stage both in the [[1994–95 Copa del Rey|Copa del Rey]] and [[1994–95 UEFA Cup|UEFA Cup]] to Valencia and [[Odense Boldklub|Odense]], respectively. The latter exit was particularly marred due to an embarrassing 0–2 home loss after a 3–2 first leg away victory.
